==English== ===Etymology=== {{root|en|ine-pro|*gʷem-}} A compound of the sources of {{af|en|be-|come}}. From {{inh|en|enm|becomen}}, {{m|enm|bicumen}}, from {{inh|en|ang|becuman|t=to come (to), approach, arrive, enter, meet with, fall in with; happen, befall; befit}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*bikwemaną||to come around, come about, come across, come by}}, equivalent to {{prefix|en|be|t1=about, around|come}}. Cognate with {{cog|sco|becum||to come, arrive, reach a destination}}, {{cog|frr|bekommen}}, {{m|frr|bykommen||to come by, obtain, receive}}, {{cog|fy|bikomme||to come by, obtain, receive}}, {{cog|nl|bekomen||to come by, obtain, receive}}, {{cog|de|bekommen||to get, receive, obtain}}, {{cog|sv|bekomma||to receive, concern}}, {{cog|got|𐌱𐌹𐌵𐌹𐌼𐌰𐌽||to come upon one, befall}}. Sense of "befit, suit" due to influence from {{ncog|enm|cweme}}, {{m|enm|icweme}}, see {{m|en|queem}}. Displaced Old English {{lang|ang|''[[weorþan]]''}}. ===Pronunciation=== * {{IPA|en|a=Southern England|/bɪˈkʌm/|/bəˈkʌm/}} * {{IPA|en|a=Northern England|/bɪˈkʊm/|/bəˈkʊm/}} * {{IPA|en|/bɪˈkʌm/|/biˈkʌm/|/bəˈkʌm/|a=US}} ** {{audio|en|en-us-become.ogg|a=California|IPA=/biˈkʌm/}} * {{IPA|en|/ˈbɪk.əm/|a=Indic}} * {{rhymes|en|ʌm|s=2}} * {{hyphenation|en|be|come}} ===Verb=== {{en-verb|become<,,became:~[dialectal],~:became[dialectal]:~n>}} # {{senseid|en|copulative}} {{lb|en|copulative|followed by an adjective or a noun}} [[begin]] to [[be]]; [[turn into]] {{q|often with permanent states}}. {{defdate|from 12th c.}} #: {{par|en|get|turn|go|come|fall|grow|wax}} #: {{ux|en|She '''became''' a doctor when she was 25.}} #: {{ux|en|The weather will '''become''' cold after the sun [[go down|goes down]].}} #: {{ux|en|The full extent of my injuries did not '''become''' evident until they tried to move me.}} #: {{ux|en|The sense ‘state or process of bearing fruit’ has '''become''' imposed on ''fruition'' as the 20c. proceeded.}} #* {{RQ:Churchill Celebrity|chapter=8|passage=The humor of my proposition appealed more strongly to Miss Trevor than I had looked for, and from that time forward she '''became''' her old self again; for, even after she had conquered her love for the Celebrity, the mortification of having been jilted by him remained.}} # {{lb|en|intransitive|archaic|_|other than in {{m|en|become of}}}} To come about; [[happen]]; come into being; [[arise]]. {{defdate|from 12th c.}} #: {{ux|en|What '''became''' of him after he was let go?}} #: {{ux|en|It hath '''becomen''' so that many a man had to sterve.}} #* {{RQ:Dunsany Time||3|And Time went forth into the worlds to obey the commands of the gods, yet he cast furtive glances at his masters, and the gods distrusted Time because he had known the worlds or ever the gods '''became'''.}} # {{senseid|en|beseem}}{{lb|en|transitive}} To be [[appropriate]] for. {{defdate|from 13th c.}} #: {{syn|en|befit|suit|beseem}} #:''It doesn’t '''become''' a true gentleman to speak in such a manner.'' #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Tempest|III|ii|text=Ay, lord, she will '''become''' thy bed, I warrant,
And bring thee forth brave [[brood]].}} #* '''1892''', {{w|Ambrose Bierce}}, “The Applicant,” in ''The Collected Works of Ambrose Bierce'', Volume II: In the Midst of Life (Tales of Soldiers and Civilians), New York: Gordian Press, 1966,[http://www.gutenberg.org/files/13334/13334-h/13334-h.htm#page281] #*: He was hatted, booted, overcoated, and umbrellaed, as '''became''' a person who was about to expose himself to the night and the storm on an errand of charity {{...}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1930|author=w:Duff Cooper|title=Talleyrand|page=7|publisher=Folio Society|year_published=2010 |passage=His ordination{{...}}enabled him to be independent of his parents, and to afford a manner of living which '''became''' his rank rather than his calling.}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} Of an adornment, piece of clothing etc.: to look [[attractive]] on (someone). {{defdate|from 14th c.}} #: {{ux|en|That dress really '''becomes''' you.}} # {{lb|en|intransitive|obsolete}} To [[arrive]], [[come]] (to a place). {{defdate|9th–18th c.}}
